scenes.title: Hook
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: close-up of the man looking straight into the camera with a knowing half smile, busy street behind him
scenes.on_screen_text: I moved to Africa to blend in. Day one, a kid called me muzungu.
scenes.text: I moved to Africa to blend in. On day one, a kid called me muzungu. Let me tell you how that happened.

scenes.title: Marcus: who I am
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: arrivals hall of Entebbe International Airport, Uganda
scenes.shot: the man talking to camera, composed, rolling suitcase beside him
scenes.text: My name is Marcus Johnson. Atlanta, Georgia. Twenty-five years of service between the Army and the federal government. I have been posted all over the world, and everywhere I went, I stood out. So when I retired, I made a plan. Uganda. My roots, a fresh start, and for once in my life, a place where I would just blend right in.

scenes.title: Arrival at Entebbe
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: outside Entebbe airport, palm trees, red earth, bright green hills
scenes.shot: the man stepping out into the sunshine wearing aviator sunglasses and bright white sneakers, smiling
scenes.text: Entebbe airport. Warm air, red earth, and green everywhere you look. I had my bags, my sunglasses, and my brand new white sneakers. I was ready.

scenes.title: Nobody stares
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: airport pickup area in Entebbe, crowd of Ugandan travellers
scenes.shot: the man standing relaxed in a crowd of people, nobody paying attention to him, content expression
scenes.text: The first thing I noticed was that nobody stared at me. In Tokyo I was a curiosity. In Germany I was the American. Here, I was nobody special. And I loved it.

scenes.title: Kato arrives
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.location: airport pickup area in Entebbe, red motorcycle parked at the curb
scenes.shot: young Ugandan boda boda rider grinning with arms wide open in welcome beside his red motorcycle
scenes.text: You are Marcus? Mama Grace sent me. I am Kato. Welcome to Uganda, my brother! Give me the small bag. The big one, you carry. I am a rider, not a lorry.

scenes.title: Marcus: where's the car?
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man looking around the car park, puzzled, holding a large suitcase
scenes.text: Kato. Good to meet you. Where is the car?

scenes.title: Kato: today we ride
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.shot: the rider patting the seat of his red motorcycle, laughing
scenes.text: Car? Ssebo, this is Kampala. The car is for people who want to arrive tomorrow. Today, we ride.

scenes.title: First boda ride
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man sitting stiffly on the back of a motorcycle taxi holding a suitcase on his knees, wide eyes
scenes.text: I have jumped out of airplanes. I have sat through budget hearings in Washington. Nothing prepared me for the back of a boda boda in Kampala traffic.

scenes.title: Kato: hold the back
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.location: busy Kampala road, motorcycle taxis and minibuses
scenes.shot: the rider looking back over his shoulder from a moving motorcycle, amused, helmet on
scenes.text: Hold on, but do not hold me like that. People will talk. Hold the back. Yes. Good. Now pray small.

scenes.title: The traffic
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: chaotic Kampala street traffic at midday
scenes.shot: busy Kampala street full of white minibus taxis, motorcycle taxis, a goat at the roadside and a man pushing a bicycle loaded with a sofa
scenes.text: Taxis, trucks, goats, a man pushing a sofa on a bicycle. Kato weaved through all of it like he could read the future.

scenes.title: Mama Grace welcomes him
scenes.speaker: Mama Grace
scenes.location: veranda of a modest Kampala compound with potted plants
scenes.shot: older Ugandan woman in a purple gomesi opening her arms in welcome on the veranda, warm smile
scenes.text: You have reached! Welcome, my son. You are most welcome. How was the journey? Are you hungry? Of course you are hungry. Sit. I have made matooke and groundnut sauce.

scenes.title: Marcus: I ate on the plane
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: veranda of a Kampala compound, plastic chairs, a low table
scenes.shot: the man raising one hand politely, slight smile, standing by a plastic chair
scenes.text: Thank you, ma'am. I actually ate on the plane.

scenes.title: Mama Grace: that was a rumor
scenes.speaker: Mama Grace
scenes.shot: the older woman in a purple gomesi pointing firmly at a chair, eyebrows raised, holding a plate of matooke
scenes.text: The plane? That was not food. That was a rumor. Sit down.

scenes.title: Lesson one
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: veranda of a Kampala compound, plate of matooke with groundnut sauce
scenes.shot: the man seated at a low table eating a large plate of matooke and groundnut sauce, resigned smile
scenes.text: Lesson one in Uganda. When Mama Grace says sit, you sit. When she says eat, the conversation is over.

scenes.title: Mama Grace: greet properly
scenes.speaker: Mama Grace
scenes.shot: the older woman in a purple gomesi wagging a finger kindly, teaching, warm smile
scenes.text: And tomorrow, you greet people properly. In Uganda we do not just say hi and walk away. You ask, how was the night? How is home? How is work? Then you listen to the answer. Greeting is not a race, my son.

scenes.title: Marcus: a full briefing
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man nodding respectfully with his hands folded on the table, slight smile
scenes.text: Yes, ma'am. Greetings are a full briefing. Understood.

scenes.title: Walking to the shops
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: red dirt road lined with small shops in a Kampala neighbourhood, afternoon
scenes.shot: the man walking confidently down the street, sunglasses on, bright white sneakers, head held high
scenes.text: That afternoon, I walked to the shops on my own. Head up, shoulders back. Just another man on the street. Blending in.

scenes.title: The boy at the stall
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: roadside fruit stall with mangoes in Kampala
scenes.shot: a small Ugandan boy standing beside a fruit stall piled with mangoes, looking up with a huge smile
scenes.text: A little boy at a roadside stall looked up from his mangoes, looked at me, and smiled the biggest smile I had ever seen.

scenes.title: Boy: Muzungu!
scenes.speaker: The boy
scenes.shot: the small boy waving excitedly with both hands, laughing
scenes.text: Muzungu! Muzungu! How are you? Muzungu, how are you?

scenes.title: Marcus: your intel is off
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man pausing, glancing down at his own forearm, then looking at the camera with a dry expression
scenes.text: Muzungu? Young man, I think your intel is off. Look at this arm. I am as African as your grandfather.

scenes.title: Boy: I am fine!
scenes.speaker: The boy
scenes.shot: the small boy grinning and giving a thumbs up
scenes.text: How are you, muzungu? I am fine!

scenes.title: The whole street joins in
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: a Ugandan street scene, a woman at a chapati stand and two men playing draughts all turning to look and laughing warmly
scenes.text: And then the whole street joined in. A lady selling chapati. Two men playing draughts. Even the chickens seemed to have an opinion.

scenes.title: Kato pulls up laughing
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.shot: the rider stopping his red motorcycle at the roadside, laughing hard, one foot on the ground
scenes.text: Marcus! They got you already? Day one! That is a new record.

scenes.title: Marcus: explain this
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man gesturing at the people around him, calm but baffled
scenes.text: Kato, explain this to me. I look exactly like everybody on this street.

scenes.title: Kato: it's the shoes
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.shot: the rider pointing down at a pair of spotless white sneakers, grinning
scenes.text: It is not your skin, my friend. It is the shoes. Those white shoes have never touched mud in their life. And the walk. You walk like you are inspecting the street. And that voice. You are one hundred percent American.

scenes.title: Marcus: nobody briefed me
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: close-up of the man, deadpan expression, one eyebrow slightly raised
scenes.text: Nobody briefed me on that.

scenes.title: Kato: the goat
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.location: roadside in Kampala, a goat nearby
scenes.shot: the rider laughing and pointing at a goat standing by the road
scenes.text: Also, you said thank you to a goat. We saw it.

scenes.title: Marcus: a polite goat
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man shrugging with dignity, glancing at a goat beside him
scenes.text: That goat was very polite to me.

scenes.title: Kato: even the goat knows
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.shot: the rider doubled over laughing on his red motorcycle
scenes.text: That goat belongs to Mama Grace. Even the goat knows you are new here.

scenes.title: Twist: Marcus adapts
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man taking off his sunglasses and holding his white sneakers in one hand, barefoot on the red earth, determined look
scenes.text: So I adapted. I took off the sunglasses. I took off the bright white sneakers. I slowed down my walk. I even tried a little Luganda.

scenes.title: Marcus: Oli otya?
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man crouching to the eye level of the small boy, friendly smile
scenes.text: Oli otya, my friend?

scenes.title: Boy: still muzungu
scenes.speaker: The boy
scenes.shot: the small boy squinting at the camera, considering, then smiling
scenes.text: Bulungi. Still muzungu.

scenes.title: Kato: it means they noticed you
scenes.speaker: Kato
scenes.location: roadside in Kampala at golden hour
scenes.shot: the rider with a friendly hand on the shoulder of the camera, warm smile, golden evening light
scenes.text: Do not worry, Marcus. Muzungu is not an insult. It means the town has noticed you. Give it time. Soon they will call you by your name.

scenes.title: Marcus: mission adjusted
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.location: veranda of a Kampala compound at sunset
scenes.shot: the man talking to camera on the veranda at sunset, relaxed, amused
scenes.text: Twenty-five years of missions, and a seven-year-old blew my cover in five seconds. Fine. Mission adjusted. Tomorrow, I learn the greetings properly. Mama Grace has already made a list.

scenes.title: Mama Grace: wear the old shoes
scenes.speaker: Mama Grace
scenes.location: veranda of a Kampala compound at dusk
scenes.shot: the older woman in a purple gomesi calling from the doorway, holding a cooking pot, playful look
scenes.text: Marcus! Come and eat. And tomorrow, wear the old shoes. The white ones are for church.

scenes.title: Closer
scenes.speaker: Marcus Johnson
scenes.shot: the man smiling at the camera with the Kampala skyline at dusk behind him
scenes.on_screen_text: Word of the day: Muzungu = foreigner. Comment: What would give YOU away?
scenes.text: Word of the day: muzungu. It means foreigner. Now tell me in the comments: what would give you away?
